content.content:
Fred,

I'm flying to LA tomorrow morning for the Griffin AGM and the Dentsu meeting, so can you take the send list for the Q4 investor update off my plate? It goes out the week after the Oct 14 board and I'll write the update itself on the plane.

Our existing investors are already on my own list. What I need from you is everyone from the bridge round who should get it, as of tonight, with the groups and details in the Q4 update send list doc so I know which paragraph each one gets. The draft update deck shows what each group gets. Get the new investors right, they'll look for their own check in it.

Please put it in your Q4 investor update folder, the README in that folder says how to name it. Then do what I put on the Existing Investor Update card in Trello. Once it's done reply here with how many firms and angels are in each group. I put Monday's review on your calendar so we can go through it together.

Robert asked about just sending it to everyone on the 2025 list. Let's not, only the people the doc says.

Thanks,
Leonard

content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2\", \"title\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\", \"name\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\", \"revisionId\": \"1b0d9b5d65\", \"createdTime\": \"2025-09-26T18:00:00Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2025-09-26T18:41:00Z\", \"text\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\\nLeonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.\\n\\nWho to look at\\nEvery name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.\\n\\nGroups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)\\nGo by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.\\nNew investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.\\nIn talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.\\nAwaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.\\nKeep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.\\nEveryone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.\\nPassed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.\\n\\\"Us\\\" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.\\nAccelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.\\n\\nBuild access\\nFor firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.\\n\\nSheet\\nOne row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.\\n\"}"}

Leonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.

Who to look at
Every name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Key Takeaways from the Pitch
• [PERSON_NAME_9160] was *most excited* about our *engine capabilities* rather than specific game titles.
• 
• Apple’s game categories:
• 
    ◦ *Cozy Games* → Targeting 7-25 y/o females (e.g., Animal Crossing players on Switch, Hello Kitty Arcade players).
    ◦ *Kid Games* → Under 7 years old, designed to keep kids engaged.
    ◦ *Classic Games* → Solitaire, Hearts, etc.
    ◦ *Match-3 Games* → Low adoption but good retention; Apple recognizes better F2P alternatives exist and won’t Push a match-3 subscription.
    ◦ *Puzzle Games* → Broad category with potential opportunities.
• *Where We Fit:*
• 
    ◦ We are positioned *between puzzle and classic games*.
    ◦ [PERSON_NAME_9160] is particularly interested in *Dominoes & Tri-Peak Solitaire*.
    ◦ *Solitaire is dominated by MobilityWare*, making it difficult to compete for Apple’s interest.
    ◦ However, a *custom-built Tri-Peak Solitaire or Dominoes game for Apple* would be a strong opportunity.
[PERSON_NAME_9160]’s Feedback on Our Games
• *Domino Delights*
•

Most major ad networks, including Google AdMob, Meta Audience Network, and Unity Ads, have strict policies against *incentivized ad views* and artificial engagement.
*Potential Policy Violations*
Here’s how your idea could violate various ad network policies:
1. *Incentivized Ad engagement (Against AdMob & Most Networks)*
    ◦ Google AdMob *explicitly prohibits* rewarding users for watching ads unless it’s a rewarded ad format tied to in-app content (e.g., extra lives, virtual currency).
    ◦ Your model directly incentivizes users to watch ads for real-world payouts, which is *not allowed*.
2. *Artificial engagement / Invalid Traffic*
    ◦ Ad networks analyze user engagement, and if they detect that people are watching ads only for money (not genuine interest), they may classify the traffic as *invalid* and withhold earnings.
    ◦ Clicks, impressions, and video views *must be organic*—forcing or incentivizing views creates *low-value interactions*, which networks can penalize.
3. *Revenue Share / Arbitrage Concerns*
    ◦ If you’re paying users a portion of ad revenue, some networks may see this as *ad arbitrage*—where the intent is not genuine app usage but merely generating ad views.
    ◦ Networks like AdMob *ban ad revenue-sharing schemes* that exist solely to funnel money to users.
4. *Bot & Fraud Detection Risks*
    ◦ Many ad networks use sophisticated fraud detection systems. If a large percentage of users are just watching ads to earn money, it could trigger *fraud flags* and get your account banned.
    ◦ Even if users are real, networks might still mark their engagement as *low-quality traffic* and *suspend payments*.
*Workarounds (If You Still Want Something Similar)*
If you still want a reward-based system, consider these alternatives:
1. *Use a Legitimate Rewarded Ad Model*
    ◦ AdMob, Unity, and other networks allow *rewarded ads* as long as the rewards stay within the app (e.g., coins, extra lives).
    ◦ You could design a game where *watching ads enhances gameplay* rather than directly giving real-world cash.
2. *Partner with Alternative Ad Networks*
    ◦ Some alternative ad networks (like Mistplay or OfferToro) specialize in *reward-based advertising*, but they typically *don’t allow direct ad revenue sharing*.
    ◦ Look into *GPT (Get Paid To) networks* that allow users to complete offers, surveys, and ad views for rewards *without violating policies*.
3. *Use Affiliate or Direct Sponsorships Instead*
    ◦ Instead of using standard ad networks, you could *partner with brands directly* and give users a cut of *affiliate revenue* (e.g., watching sponsored videos, completing brand challenges).
*Bottom Line*

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

"message", "text": "Progress summary \u2014 Harmony Games Engine and traction\n*Where the engine is today*\n Harmony Games Engine is our reusable production platform that puts AI in the loop for level creation, adaptive difficulty, content scheduling, economy tuning, analytics, and rapid creative testing. v1 took ~15 months to build. We now port the stack into a new title in about 4 months at production quality, so a small team can learn faster and reuse success.\n*Engine progression*\n\u2022 *Phase 1 (complete):* AI as assistant. Standardized live service infrastructure, level gen prototypes, physics-based 3D puzzle layer, boosters, leaderboards, quests, calendars, season pass. Goal was to harden the backbone.\n\u2022 *Phase 2 (in flight):* AI as junior designer. Automated level generation with constraints, difficulty scoring, authorable event tooling, experiment harness, and self-serve tools for designers. Live service personalization and faster iteration loops. Current status in Zombie Match: service integration ~60% complete with trophy path, leaderboards, quests, daily gift, teams online or in final integration. Creative pipeline from concept to first testable video in about 2 hours.\n\u2022 *Next (12 months):* Data-driven designer. Use live player data and reinforcement learning to adapt difficulty, rewards, and pacing. Move service execution toward \u201cautopilot\u201d with embedded analytics optimizing events across titles with human guidance.\n*Traction and revenue*\n\u2022 *Domino Delights (live in small markets):*\n\u2022  \u2022 Avg daily playtime: *~30 minutes*\n\u2022  \u2022 Avg DAU over last 6 months: *~600*\n\u2022  \u2022 ARPDAU: *~$0.10*\n\u2022  \u2022 Earlier retention reads landed below our scale bar (D7 in mid-teens, ~35% of D1), which capped LTV against CPI. We are not scaling this title. Domino Delights validated the engine\u2019s content pipeline, physics, boosters, event systems, storefront, and offer framework. The game is now being positioned with a publisher while we reuse the stack on a better core.\n\u2022 *Zombie Match 3D (alpha, UK iOS tests):*\n\u2022  \u2022 Early signals at minimal polish: *~34% D1*, *~23 min day-0 playtime*, *~$4.50 CPI* (small n)\n\u2022  \u2022 Live service integration ~60% complete, with remaining features on a short horizon\n\u2022  \u2022 Next 4\u20136 weeks: expand to *500+ levels*, complete polish/VFX, and scale tests to *2\u20133k* users for stable reads\n\u2022  \u2022 Gates to proceed: *\u226545% D1*, *\u226545% D7/D1*, *\u2264$3.50 CPI* in UK iOS. We scale only if the data clears these bars.\n*Why this matters*\n The engine lets us compress concept-to-beta cycles, cut net-new code, and operate multiple shots on goal with a lean team. Domino Delights proved the platform. Zombie Match applies it to a distinct Match & Slash core aimed at Western audiences. The bridge focuses on finishing Phase 2 capabilities and driving Zombie Match from alpha into beta and soft launch with disciplined, data-led gates.", "channel": "C096HFA5Z8W", "user": Our mission is simple: take many high-quality shots on goal, move fast, and scale only when the data says we\u2019ve earned it.\n\nAt the center is Harmony Games Engine\u2014our reusable production platform that puts AI in the loop for level creation, adaptive difficulty, event scheduling (the \u201clive service\u201d layer), economy tuning, analytics, and creative testing. v1 took ~15 months to build; now we can port the stack into a new title in ~4 months with production quality. The result is fewer one-off builds, faster iteration, and a small team that learns cheaper than traditional studios.\n\nOur first franchise with a break-through potential is Zombie Match 3D, introducing a new \u201cMatch & Slash\u201d subgenre: fast 3D matching where every match becomes a weapon, layered with items, upgrades, bosses, and horde modes. The game is live in early tests (alpha) with a growing content slate and service layer. Early UK iOS signals on minimal polish: ~34% day-one retention and ~25 minutes first-day playtime with only 100 levels and minimal polish. Over the next 4\u20136 weeks we\u2019ll expand to 500+ levels, add more polish/VFX, and scale tests to 2\u20133k users. Go/No-Go gates are explicit: \u226545% day-one retention, \u226545% day-seven-to-day-one retention ratio, and \u2264$3.50 CPI in UK iOS. We scale only if we clear the gates. If not, we\u2019ll pivot to our next title\n\nOn the platform roadmap, we\u2019re evolving AI from \u201cassistant\u201d to \u201cjunior designer\u201d toward a data-driven designer that adapts difficulty, rewards, and pacing from live player data. On the service side, our event/offer system already supports leaderboards, quests, calendars, and season passes, with personalization and rapid experiment tooling next.\n\nWe\u2019re raising a $2.5M seed extension for extending runway ~18+ months while we: (1) complete the next Harmony Games Engine milestones and content pipeline ($1.5M), and (2) fund beta and soft-launch user acquisition that will be only used if metrics justify the marketing spend ($1.0M). ----- Wed, 17 Sep 2025 14:15:12 -0700 | From: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> | To: PERSON_0787_NAME <PERSON_0787_EMAIL> | Cc: robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> | Subj: Re: GFR Fund <> [SOURCE_ORG_0001]
Hi PERSON_0787_NAME,

Great to meet a fellow ex-GREE! I have very fond memories of the 300 Berry
office, and my time There shaped a lot of my early growth in my career. I
wasn't aware that the GFR fund was associated with GREE, such a pleasant
surprise!

I booked the earliest time on your calendar. If it is helpful, I would be
happy to share an additional overview of the team, company, and roadmap
ahead of our chat.

If you also have the bandwidth, please check out our innovative new Puzzle
RPG, Zombie Match iOS alpha:
https://apps.Apple.com/us/app/zombie-match-3d/id6743495619

Looking forward to our conversation,

Best,
Leonard
----- Wed, 17 Sep 2025 17:08:43 -0700 | From: PERSON_0787_NAME <PERSON_0787_EMAIL> | To: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> | Cc: robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> | Subj: Re: GFR Fund <> [SOURCE_ORG_0001]
Thanks for the follow up Leonard!

I started as a new grad as [USERNAME_23653]!!
Excited to see what you are looking towards.

Talk to you in a while!
----- Thu, 18 Sep 2025 11:13:00 -0700 | From: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> | To: PERSON_0787_NAME <PERSON_0787_EMAIL> | Cc: robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> | Subj: Re: GFR Fund <> [SOURCE_ORG_0001]
Hi PERSON_0787_NAME,

I had to move the meeting to Tuesday Sep 30th because our CTO is traveling
on Monday Sep 29th. Please feel free to cancel the one scheduled for Monday
- I don't have permission to remove it.

Best regards,
Leonard
----- Sat, 20 Sep 2025 10:03:42 +0900 | From: PERSON_0787_NAME <PERSON_0787_EMAIL> | To: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> | Cc: robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> | Subj: Re: GFR Fund <> [SOURCE_ORG_0001]
Sounds good, thanks!
----- Tue, 30 Sep 2025 18:41:38 -0700 | From: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> | To: PERSON_0787_NAME <PERSON_0787_EMAIL> | Cc: robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> | Subj: Re: GFR Fund <> [SOURCE_ORG_0001]
Hi PERSON_0787_NAME,

It was great chatting with a top 200 Pokémon player and investor today and
learning about the GFR fund. Per our conversation, I wanted to follow up
with one request and two supplementary materials:

   1.

   *Next games:* [PERSON_NAME_0054] will expand on this, but I wanted to share the
   material I mentioned earlier about our puzzle engine capabilities and the
   game genres we can move into quickly. Please see the attached puzzle engine
   roadmap doc.
   2.

   *Engine strategy:* You asked about our engine strategy. I’m sharing our
   long-term vision deck on that front. Happy to go deeper into what the
   next-generation AI-powered publisher will look like in a follow-up meeting.
   This deck is separate from our main pitch not because of a lack of
   ambition, but because we recognize that building successful games first is
   essential to continuing our engine development. In the near term, we’re
   prioritizing what helps us move faster.
   3.

   *Access to Zombie Match:* What’s your email address so I can add you to
   our Google Play account? Zombie Match is available in the US App Store, but
   if this download link doesn’t work, please share your email:

   [URL_11306]

Looking forward to hearing from you next week.

Best regards,
Leonard

----- Sat, 20 Sep 2025 10:03:42 +0900 | From: PERSON_0787_NAME <PERSON_0787_EMAIL> | To: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> | Cc: robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> | Subj: Re: GFR Fund <> [SOURCE_ORG_0001]

----- Tue, 30 Sep 2025 18:41:38 -0700 | From: leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> | To: PERSON_0787_NAME <PERSON_0787_EMAIL> | Cc: robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> | Subj: Re: GFR Fund <> [SOURCE_ORG_0001]
Hi PERSON_0787_NAME,

It was great chatting with a top 200 Pokémon player and investor today and
learning about the GFR fund. Per our conversation, I wanted to follow up
with one request and two supplementary materials:

   1.

   *Next games:* [PERSON_NAME_0054] will expand on this, but I wanted to share the
   material I mentioned earlier about our puzzle engine capabilities and the
   game genres we can move into quickly. Please see the attached puzzle engine
   roadmap doc.
   2.

   *Engine strategy:* You asked about our engine strategy. I’m sharing our
   long-term vision deck on that front. Happy to go deeper into what the
   next-generation AI-powered publisher will look like in a follow-up meeting.
   This deck is separate from our main pitch not because of a lack of
   ambition, but because we recognize that building successful games first is
   essential to continuing our engine development. In the near term, we’re
   prioritizing what helps us move faster.
   3.

   *Access to Zombie Match:* What’s your email address so I can add you to
   our Google Play account? Zombie Match is available in the US App Store, but
   if this download link doesn’t work, please share your email:

   [URL_11306]

Looking forward to hearing from you next week.

Best regards,
Leonard

The engine lets a lean team ship faster, test more cheaply, and scale potential hits. We build hit-ready puzzle RPGs for Western mobile players and partner studios, with our first franchise being a Match & Slash puzzle RPG with day-one liveops. We monetize through free-to-play in-app purchases and ads, and selectively pursue revenue-share partnerships with large publishing partners.\\n\\n*Stage:* Engine-first mobile game studio focused on puzzle RPGs; bridge/seed extension. For a quick demo of our engine please visit 1- Harmony Games Puzzle Engine: <https://youtu.be/kgcL7xexAAk> 2-Harmony Games Liveops Engine: <https://youtu.be/8gEsoDoaW3Q>\\nTraction: Domino Delights shipped; Match & Slash puzzle RPG in active development with day-one live ops. I've done all three things Leonard asked, well ahead of Monday's review. As he defined it, the list covers the bridge round as of end of day Sep 30 (Pacific).

**Count by group**
| Group | Firms | Angels |
|---|---|---|
| New investor | 0 | 1 (Anton Bernstein, $25K; DocuSign "Completed" notice Sep 26) |
| In talks | 8 (GFR Fund, SciPlay, Dentsu Ventures, NCsoft, a16z, T-Accelerate, Homa, Brightwater Games Fund) | 0 |
| Awaiting reply | 14 | 0 |
| Keep warm | 2 (LVP, Hiro Capital; both said no after a call) | 0 |

**What's done**
- **Send list:** a Google Sheet called "Q4 update - send list", named the way the folder's README asks. It's in your Q4 2025 investor update folder and shared with Leonard. It has one row per firm or angel, with group, amount, build access and the reason for each placement.
- **Trello card:** I added New investor, In talks and Awaiting reply checklists to the Existing Investor Update card, one item per firm or angel.
- **Follow-up cards:** I created 19 "F/up with …" cards in To Do. Dentsu and Makers Fund don't get one because they already have calls on your calendar (Oct 1 and Oct 8). NCsoft already had a To Do card, so I commented on that instead.
- **Reply to Leonard:** sent on his thread with the counts above. Robert and Arthur were cc'd on his email, but my reply only went to Leonard.

**Decisions to check on Monday**
- **Paul Heydon is off the list.** He agreed to $50K but never signed, and on Sep 30 he told Leonard he can't invest this year.
- **Others left off:** Play Ventures, because their no went to Griffin and we never had a call. Mattel, because it was only an RFP conversation. Grishin, 1AM Gaming and Lakestar, because they said no without a call.
- **a16z stays In talks.** Their speedrun rejection doesn't count as an answer on the bridge.
- **Hiro Capital is Keep warm, not Awaiting reply.** The partner who said no on Sep 26 after the Sep 23 call is from Hiro.
- **Build access is iOS only for Dentsu, NCsoft, T-Accelerate and Brightwater.** The Linear log says they also got Android access, but Arthur posted on Sep 30 that the Android tester list was never attached. GFR, SciPlay, Homa and a16z have no build access.
- **Keep warm checklist:** none existed on the card, so I created one with LVP and Hiro. Leonard's Sep 14 note says passes after a call go on it. His latest note asked for checklists for the other three groups, so delete it if he didn't want it.

Sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/17ievH-2sAicSlHIdm6V2rFOfLUBWv58pwYSaD-oB7Vw/edit
